question.prompt: The missing-genre 404 test needs a slug value that is guaranteed not to match any real genre. How should this run supply it?

options.label: Keep variable
options.detail: Keep `{{nonexistent_genre_slug}}` in the test and fill it with a guaranteed-missing slug before execution.

options.label: Provide slug
options.detail: Type a concrete slug that is guaranteed not to match any real genre and replace `{{nonexistent_genre_slug}}` with it.

options.label: Rework test data
options.detail: Edit the negative test to use a different owner-supplied way of reaching a non-existent genre URL.

content.risk_rationale: If the missing-genre slug accidentally matches a real genre, the negative test stops proving the 404 contract and could pass or fail for the wrong reason. The source promised the 404 outcome but did not supply a concrete invalid slug value.

# Genre listing shows default controls and complete book-tile metadata

> Prove that an existing genre listing shows `<total> book(s) found` for all genre matches, defaults to `Title (A-Z)`, and each displayed tile shows a cover image, linked title, author, `Rating: <n>`, and format.

## Step 1

Open http://127.0.0.1:5050/books in a fresh browser session.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-14, ac-15, ac-16, ac-17, ac-18, ac-19, ac-20

On `/books`, open the first visible genre link to reach a valid genre listing page, then assert the listing shows visible text matching `<number> book(s) found`, the selected sort option is `Title (A-Z)`, the sort control also offers `Rating (high to low)`, the selected `Show` value is 20, the `Show` control offers exactly 6, 12, and 20, and visible `Grid view` and `List view` controls are present.

## Step 3 @verifies ac-1, ac-2, ac-3, ac-4, ac-5, ac-6, ac-7, ac-8

On the same genre listing page, inspect every displayed book tile and the surrounding published-books surface, then assert each visible tile shows a cover image, the title as a link, author text, rating text beginning with `Rating: `, and format text, and that no visible price amounts, basket controls, or checkout actions appear anywhere on the page.

    objective: On `/books`, open the first visible genre link to reach a valid genre listing page, then assert the listing shows visible text matching `<number> book(s) found`, the selected sort option is `Title (A-Z)`, the sort control also offers `Rating (high to low)`, the selected `Show` value is 20, the `Show` control offers exactly 6, 12, and 20, and visible `Grid view` and `List view` controls are present.

    step: 3

# Catalog landing page shows catalog totals, genre counts, and genre links

> Prove that `/books` states the total catalog size, lists every genre with its title count, and each genre name links to a genre listing page.

## Step 1

Open http://127.0.0.1:5050/books in a fresh browser session.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-9, ac-1, ac-2, ac-3

On the `/books` page, inspect the published-books catalog summary, then assert there is visible text matching `<number> books published through Fernwood Press so far.` and no visible price amounts, basket controls, or checkout actions appear anywhere in the published-books area.

## Step 3 @verifies ac-10, ac-11

On the same `/books` page, inspect every visible genre entry in the genre list, then assert each displayed genre entry shows a title count and the genre name is rendered as a link with a non-empty destination different from the current `/books` URL.
content.objectives_blob:
objectives:
  - objective: Open http://127.0.0.1:5050/books in a fresh browser session.
    step: 1
  - check:
      expected_mode: authored
      kind: presence
      operand: visible text matching `<total> books published through Fernwood Press so far.`
      operator: exists
      review_required: false
      verified_against: ac-9
    objective: On the `/books` page, inspect the published-books catalog summary, then assert there is visible text matching `<number> books published through Fernwood Press so far.` and no visible price amounts, basket controls, or checkout actions appear anywhere in the published-books area.
    step: 2
    verifies:
      - ac-9
      - ac-1
      - ac-2
      - ac-3
  - objective: On the same `/books` page, inspect every visible genre entry in the genre list, then assert each displayed genre entry shows a title count and the genre name is rendered as a link with a non-empty destination different from the current `/books` URL.
    step: 3
    verifies:
      - ac-10
      - ac-11
scenario: Browse the catalog landing page and enter a genre listing
title: Catalog landing page shows catalog totals, genre counts, and genre links

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Score 98: automates the core valid-genre listing path and covers the largest set of user-visible promises: found count, default sort, available sort and page-size controls, layout controls, showcase-only behavior, and complete tile metadata.

[value_score] Score 96: automates the required negative path for missing genres and proves both the 404 response and exact fallback message while also checking the showcase-only constraints on the error page.

[value_score] Score 94: automates the public catalog entry path on `/books`, covering the catalog-size statement, per-genre counts, navigable genre links, and showcase-only constraints on the landing page.

[self_critique] Oracle fit and over-breadth: kept this test to the default-state genre listing and did not claim rating reordering, page-size switching, or grid/list parity, because those outcome-changing promises were budget-evicted as separate scenarios and would have over-broadened the assertions here.

[self_critique] Technique fit and negative coverage: this test remained the dedicated negative path for a non-existent genre and used a derived invalid URL from a real genre link so the route shape comes from the app under test rather than an invented path pattern.

[self_critique] Oracle fit and technique fit: this test proved the `/books` landing-page summary and genre-directory promises with visible-text and link-destination observables, avoiding assumptions about a specific genre slug or genre-listing content that belonged to other scenarios.
